mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in WORKPLACES mobility (from -25.9% to -13.9%) signals progressive workplace reopening. This restores commuting routines and weekday retail visitation patterns, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 12 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 5 percentage points in week 1 of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 16.4% to 10.6%) indicates residents are spending less time at home, reallocating time to out-of-home activities. This behavioral shift directly increases RETAIL_REC visits over the next two weeks as the trend accelerates.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 11% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 5.8 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stabilizes or rises above 12% while RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines in the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains depressed (at -23.0%) but shows consistent improvement trend. When TRANSIT recovers by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week, it signals confidence in public transport safety, enabling retail foot traffic to surge within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 8.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week of a TRANSIT improvement of 3+ percentage points, or TRANSIT reverses by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (11.6–12.7% above baseline) combined with declining RESIDENTIAL (10.6%) indicates essential shopping trips are maintained while discretionary out-of-home time increases. This dual signal drives RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks through substitution of home time for retail visits.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 11% AND RESIDENTIAL falls below 11%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 10% in any week.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained depression in PARKS mobility (at -29.3%) signals outdoor recreation restrictions remain in place. When PARKS mobility begins to recover, it indicates policy relaxation that simultaneously permits retail reopening, causing RETAIL_REC to rise within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained depressed at -29.3% in most recent week
failure_condition: PARKS does not improve by 2+ percentage points in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of WORKPLACES recovery (improving 12 points over four weeks) and TRANSIT recovery (improving 8.7 points) creates a reinforcing cycle: workplace return drives transit demand, which signals safe commuting, which attracts retail visitors. This interaction effect accelerates RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by more than 2 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series show consistent four-week improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September marks the start of autumn retail season in Hong Kong. Combined with observed four-week improvement trend across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and declining RESIDENTIAL, seasonal demand for retail goods amplifies the activity-driven recovery, producing above-baseline RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline in week 1 of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent gap between GROCERY_PHARM (above baseline at +11.6%) and RETAIL_REC (below baseline at -21.9%) indicates consumers prioritize essential shopping while avoiding discretionary retail. As confidence builds (signaled by WORKPLACES recovery), this gap narrows and RETAIL_REC rises toward GROCERY_PHARM levels over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 3 percentage points AND gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC exceeds 30 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:33.5 percentage point gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC in most recent week
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC does not narrow by at least 5 percentage points over the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC declines further.
